subject: biology-2
question: **HIV** infects CD4 helper T cells and uses the cells' machinery to produce more virus particles. Which sequence best matches the HIV life cycle?

options.text: Attachment, immediate lysis of the cell, release, then infection of nearby cells.
Conversion of DNA into RNA, then assembly of new capsids inside the nucleus.
Attachment and entry, reverse transcription of RNA into DNA, integration into the host chromosome, then production and release of new particles.
Integration of viral proteins into the cell membrane, then passive diffusion of whole viruses out of the cell.

explanation: HIV attaches to CD4 helper T cells, enters, reverse transcribes its RNA into DNA, integrates that DNA into the host chromosome, and later produces new particles that bud from the cell. B has the direction reversed, because reverse transcription makes DNA from RNA, not the other way. A is wrong because HIV buds off rather than lysing the cell immediately. D is wrong because new viruses assemble inside the cell, and they do not diffuse out whole.
